jamie.r: Hey folks, need help. My partner's kid (stepchild) moved in with us full-time last week. Can I add them to my benefits midyear? What's the process and what docs are needed?

maria.peopleops: Hi Jamie 1a: welcome to People Ops. Yes, a permanent move-in/change in household can be a QLE. You have 30 days from the date the child became your dependent to submit the QLE and docs.

jamie.r: Sweet. Do I need custody papers? We're not changing legal custody, just physical residence.

maria.peopleops: Legal custody helps but isn't required if the qualifying reason is residency. Acceptable docs include:
- School enrollment showing child at your address
- DMV or government ID with the child's address
- Signed notarized statement from the custodial parent + proof of shared residence (lease or utility bill)
- Temporary guardianship or placement agreement also works

jamie.r: If I upload a school enrollment + a signed note from the other parent, is that usually enough?

maria.peopleops: Usually yes. We may submit those to the carrier; some carriers ask for more. If carrier requests additional proof well notify you. You can upload via People Ops portal > Benefits > QLE uploads or email benefits@redwood.com with subject: "QLE: Add dependent - stepchild - <Jamie R>".

benefits-bot: Acknowledged uploads will generate a case number and carrier verification typically takes 3-10 business days. If you upload now we will return a case ID.

jamie.r: Payroll question: if added mid-pay-period, how is deduction handled?

lisa.payroll: Payroll here. Deductions depend on the carrier effective date. If carrier makes coverage effective on the move-in date and it's within our payroll cutoff, we prorate for the pay period. If the carrier's effective date is 1st of next month, you won't see retro proration. We can estimate after carrier confirms.

jamie.r: Is there any chance premiums are charged retroactively to the event date?

lisa.payroll: Yes if the carrier accepts the retro effective date and we get confirmation before payroll locks, payroll will post a prorated amount or an adjustment depending on timing. We'll flag your case for review if you note the urgency.

jamie.r: Are dependents on step-parent additions covered for all plans (medical/dental/vision)?

maria.peopleops: Carriers vary. Core medical typically allows stepchild additions under QLEs; some dental/vision carriers require additional verification. We will pass documents to each carrier and share their responses.

jamie.r: Any impact on FSA/HSA enrollment? I didn't enroll my spouse but I have HSA.

maria.peopleops: Adding a dependent doesn't change HSA eligibility for you, but you can adjust contribution amounts if needed during the QLE. For FSAs, adding a dependent may allow you to enroll in dependent care FSA midyear if eligible. We'll include FSA/HSA teams in the case notes.

jamie.r: My partner's coverage exists. How does coordination work?
eve.broker: If the child is covered on another plan, COB rules apply. Usually the child's primary coverage is determined by parent order; step-parent status doesn't change COB automatically. If your plan becomes primary, claims should go there first; otherwise secondary will coordinate. We can help with claims coordination if needed.

jamie.r: One more: what's the turnaround if carrier asks for more docs? I have an appt in nine days.
maria.peopleops: If carrier requests additional docs we typically have 3-5 business days to respond; carriers may expedite for urgent care. For your appt, DM me the provider + date and we'll request a predetermination/coverage letter to present at the visit.

jamie.r: Uploading school enrollment and signed note now. tagging benefits@redwood.com

benefits-bot: Upload received. Case #RB-2217 created. Expect carrier verif in 3-7 business days. If you need predetermination, please reply with provider name and appt date.

maria.peopleops: Thanks Jamie. Ping here after upload if you want us to nudge payroll/expedite a coverage letter. We'll track and post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
